question.problem: Find the point(s) of the intersection of the ellipsoid $\frac{{x}^{2}}{27}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{3}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{3}=1$ and the line $\frac{x-3}{3}=y-1=z-1.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we write the equation of our line in parametric form:

$$
\frac{x-3}{3}=y-1=z-1=t\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}x=3t+3 \\ y=t+1 \\ z=t+1,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Substituting the above expressions for $x$, $y$, and $z$ into the equation of the ellipsoid, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{27}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{3}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{3} & =1 \\ {x}^{2}+9{y}^{2}+9{z}^{2} & =27 \\ (3t+3)^{2}+9(t+1)^{2}+9(t+1)^{2} & =27 \\ (9{t}^{2}+18t+9)+9({t}^{2}+2t+1)+9({t}^{2}+2t+1) & =27 \\ 27{t}^{2}+54t+27 & =27 \\ 27{t}^{2}+54t & =0 \\ {t}^{2}+2t & =0 \\ t(t+2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we get the solutions $t=0$ and $t=-2.$ 

Now, we substitute our solutions back into the equations of the line.

- For $t=0$, we have

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=3(0)+3=3 \\ y=(0)+1=1 \\ z=(0)+1=1,\end{aligned}
$$

so the first point is $(3,1,1).$

- For $t=-2$, we have

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=3(-2)+3=-3 \\ y=(-2)+1=-1 \\ z=(-2)+1=-1,\end{aligned}
$$

so the second point is $(-3,-1,-1).$

Therefore, the points of intersection are $(3,1,1)$ and $(-3,-1,-1).$
